body: The trigger was a **2016–17 business inflection**. In early 2017 Radico had ₹742 crore of net debt and had "not performed well in the last two years due to increasing raw material costs" ([Angel Broking 3QFY17](https://www.angelone.in/get-html-report/AngelBrokingResearch_Radico%20Khaitan_3QFY2017RU_130217.html)). Over the next four years **debt/equity fell from 0.77 to 0.15**, and revenue grew 44% while **PAT grew 239%**, from ₹80 crore to ₹271 crore ([StockEdge](https://blog.stockedge.com/stock-insights-radico-khaitan-ltd/)). That is operating leverage driven by a premium mix. By FY26, consolidated PAT had risen 74.6% to ₹602.5 crore, and Prestige & Above brands made up more than half of operating revenue ([AlphaStreet](https://alphastreet.com/india/radico-khaitan-premiumization-drives-strong-growth-outlook)). A rough decomposition (the share count is unverified, so confirm on screener.in) runs as follows. From an FY17 trough near ₹110 to about ₹4,200 is roughly 38x. **PAT grew about 7.5x** while **trailing P/E rerated about 5x**, from the high teens to 90x+. That is Chris Mayer's "twin engine": earnings growth multiplied by a rising multiple ([Validea on Mayer](https://blog.validea.com/?p=33794)). The early signals visible in 2016–17 were premium-brand volume growth while regular brands stagnated, management guiding to debt reduction without big new capex, and a reversal of the raw-material cost cycle. Two further elements are plausible but **unverified as documented contemporaneous theses**: USL's distraction during the Diageo transition leaving room for challengers, and the luxury launches (Rampur single malt, Jaisalmer gin), whose launch years are also unverified.
